First, we can simplify the limit using trigonometric identities, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\theta \operatorname{csc}⁡\theta } & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\theta }÷\operatorname{csc}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\theta }÷\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Let's now evaluate the limits separately:

- Consider the first limit. Notice that as $\theta \to 0,$ both numerator and denominator approach $0.$ 

So, if we attempt to evaluate the limit directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=\frac{0}{0},
$$

which is an indeterminate form. 

Instead, let's recall the following special limit:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }=1\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider the second limit. Evaluating it directly, we get

$$
{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\operatorname{cos}⁡0=1.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\theta }\cdot {lim}_{\theta \to 0}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =1\cdot 1=1.\end{aligned}
$$
